<div class="grid lg:grid-cols-2 gap-8 lg:gap-16"><div class="w-full min-w-full"><p>Manage your Supabase organizations and projects programmatically.</p><h2 id="authentication" class="group scroll-mt-24">Authentication<a href="#authentication" class="ml-2 opacity-0 focus:opacity-100 group-hover:opacity-100 transition">#</a></h2><p>All API requests require an access token to be included in the Authorization header: <code>Authorization Bearer <access_token></code>.</p><p>There are two ways to generate an access token:</p><ol>
<li>
<p><strong>Personal access token (PAT):</strong>
PATs are tokens with a custom expiry that you manually generate to access the Management API. They are useful for automating workflows or developing against the Management API. PATs carry the same privileges as your user account, so be sure to keep it secret.</p>
<p>To generate or manage your personal access tokens, visit your <a href="/dashboard/account/tokens" class="underline transition underline-offset-2 decoration-inherit hover:decoration-foreground text-inherit hover:text-foreground">account</a> page.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>OAuth2:</strong>
OAuth2 allows your application to generate tokens on behalf of a Supabase user, providing secure and limited access to their account without requiring their credentials. Use this if you're building a third-party app that needs to create or manage Supabase projects on behalf of your users. Tokens generated via OAuth2 are short-lived and tied to specific scopes to ensure your app can only perform actions that are explicitly approved by the user.</p>
<p>See <a href="/docs/guides/integrations/build-a-supabase-integration" class="underline transition underline-offset-2 decoration-inherit hover:decoration-foreground text-inherit hover:text-foreground">Build a Supabase Integration</a> to set up OAuth2 for your application.</p>
</li>
</ol><div class="shiki group relative not-prose w-full overflow-x-auto border border-default rounded-lg bg-200 text-sm" role="group" aria-roledescription="code block"><div class="opacity-0 flex HTTPS.</p><h2 id="rate-limits" class="group scroll-mt-24">Rate limits<a href="#rate-limits" class="ml-2 opacity-0 focus:opacity-100 group-hover:opacity-100 transition">#</a></h2><p>Rate limits are applied to prevent abuse and ensure fair usage of the Management API. Rate limits are based on a per-user, per-scope model, meaning each user gets independent rate limits for each project and organization they interact with.</p><h3 id="standard-rate-limit" class="group scroll-mt-24">Standard rate limit<a href="#standard-rate-limit" class="ml-2 opacity-0 focus:opacity-100 group-hover:opacity-100 transition">#</a></h3><table><thead><tr><th>Limit</th><th>Duration</th><th>Scope</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>120 requests</td><td>1 minute</td><td>Per user, per project/organization</td></tr></tbody></table><p>When you exceed this rate limit, all subsequent API calls will return a <code>429 Too Many Requests</code> response for the remainder of the minute. Once the time window expires, your request quota resets and you can make requests again.</p><h3 id="rate-limit-scope" class="group scroll-mt-24">Rate limit scope<a href="#rate-limit-scope" class="ml-2 opacity-0 focus:opacity-100 group-hover:opacity-100 transition">#</a></h3><p>Rate limits are applied with per-user + per-scope isolation:</p><ul>
<li><strong>Project scope</strong>: Rate limits apply independently to each project. Requests to one project do not count toward the limit of another project.</li>
<li><strong>Organization scope</strong>: Rate limits apply independently to each organization. Requests to one organization do not count toward the limit of another organization.</li>
</ul><p>This means you can make 120 requests to Project A and 120 requests to Project B within the same minute without hitting rate limits, as they are tracked separately.</p><h3 id="rate-limit-response-headers" class="group scroll-mt-24">Rate limit response headers<a href="#rate-limit-response-headers" class="ml-2 opacity-0 focus:opacity-100 group-hover:opacity-100 transition">#</a></h3><p>Every API response includes rate limit information following official <a href="https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-ietf-httpapi-ratelimit-headers" aria-label="External Source: HTTP specification headers" class="underline transition underline-offset-2 decoration-inherit hover:decoration-foreground text-inherit hover:text-foreground">HTTP specification headers<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="14" height="14" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-external-link inline-block align-[-1px] ml-0.5 text-lighter" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M15 3h6v6"></path><path d="M10 14 21 3"></path><path d="M18 13v6a2 2 0 0 1-2 2H5a2 2 0 0 1-2-2V8a2 2 0 0 1 2-2h6"></path></svg></a>:</p><ul>
<li><code>X-RateLimit-Limit</code> - The maximum number of requests allowed in the current time window</li>
<li><code>X-RateLimit-Remaining</code> - The number of requests remaining before you hit the rate limit</li>
<li><code>X-RateLimit-Reset</code> - The number of seconds remaining until your rate limit resets</li>
</ul><p>You can use these headers to monitor your usage and implement proactive rate limit handling before receiving a 429 response.</p><h3 id="how-rate-limits-are-tracked" class="group scroll-mt-24">How rate limits are tracked<a href="#how-rate-limits-are-tracked" class="ml-2 opacity-0 focus:opacity-100 group-hover:opacity-100 transition">#</a></h3><p>Your requests are identified and tracked using one of the following identifiers, in this order of priority:</p><ol>
<li><strong>OAuth App ID</strong> - If your request is authenticated via an OAuth application</li>
<li><strong>User ID</strong> - If your request is authenticated with a personal access token</li>
<li><strong>IP Address</strong> - If your request is unauthenticated (extracted from request headers)</li>
</ol><p>Each identifier is combined with the scope (project or organization) to create a unique tracking key. This ensures that rate limits are isolated per user and per scope, preventing one project or organization from affecting another.</p><h3 id="endpoint-exceptions" class="group scroll-mt-24">Endpoint exceptions<a href="#endpoint-exceptions" class="ml-2 opacity-0 focus:opacity-100 group-hover:opacity-100 transition">#</a></h3><p>Some endpoints have stricter rate limits than the standard 120 requests per minute to prevent abuse of resource-intensive operations:</p><table><thead><tr><th>Endpoint</th><th>Limit</th><th>Duration</th><th>Reason</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><code>GET /v1/projects/:ref/endpoints/logs.all</code></td><td>30 requests</td><td>1 minute</td><td>Analytics log queries are computationally expensive</td></tr><tr><td><code>GET /v1/projects/:ref/endpoints/usage.api-counts</code></td><td>30 requests</td><td>1 minute</td><td>Analytics aggregation is computationally expensive</td></tr><tr><td><code>GET /v1/projects/:ref/endpoints/usage.api-requests-count</code></td><td>30 requests</td><td>1 minute</td><td>Analytics aggregation is computationally expensive</td></tr><tr><td><code>GET /v1/projects/:ref/database/context</code></td><td>10 requests</td><td>1 minute</td><td>Database context operations are resource-intensive</td></tr><tr><td><code>GET /v1/projects/:ref/database/context</code></td><td>1 request</td><td>1 second</td><td>Burst limit to prevent rapid successive requests</td></tr><tr><td><code>POST /v1/projects/:ref/config/custom-hostname/initialize</code></td><td>10 requests</td><td>1 minute</td><td>These operations are expensive</td></tr><tr><td><code>POST /v1/projects/:ref/config/custom-hostname/reverify</code></td><td>10 requests</td><td>1 minute</td><td>These operations are expensive</td></tr><tr><td><code>DELETE /v1/projects/:ref/config/custom-hostname</code></td><td>10 requests</td><td>1 minute</td><td>These operations are expensive</td></tr><tr><td><code>GET /v1/projects/:ref/config/vanity-subdomain</code></td><td>10 requests</td><td>1 minute</td><td>These operations are expensive</td></tr></tbody></table><p><strong>Note:</strong> The <code>GET /v1/projects/:ref/database/context</code> endpoint has dual rate limiting. You can make up to 10 requests per minute, but also no more than 1 request per second to prevent burst traffic.</p><p>Some endpoints have the standard 120 requests per minute but with different timeout durations:</p><table><thead><tr><th>Endpoint</th><th>Limit</th><th>Duration</th><th>Reason</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><code>POST /v1/projects/:ref/database/migrations</code></td><td>120 requests</td><td>3 minutes</td><td>Database migrations may require more processing time</td></tr></tbody></table><h3 id="best-practices" class="group scroll-mt-24">Best practices<a href="#best-practices" class="ml-2 opacity-0 focus:opacity-100 group-hover:opacity-100 transition">#</a></h3><ul>
<li><strong>Monitor rate limit headers</strong> - Check the <code>X-RateLimit-Remaining</code> header to see how many requests you have left. When it approaches 0, slow down your requests to avoid hitting the limit.</li>
<li><strong>Implement exponential backoff</strong> - When you receive a 429 response, wait before retrying. You can use the <code>X-RateLimit-Reset</code> header (seconds) to determine exactly how long to wait.</li>
<li><strong>Batch operations</strong> - Where possible, combine multiple operations into fewer API calls to reduce your request count.</li>
<li><strong>Be mindful of expensive endpoints</strong> - Analytics, database context, and domain endpoints have stricter limits, so use them judiciously.</li>
</ul><p>The Management API is subject to our fair-use policy. All resources created via the API are subject to the pricing detailed on our <a href="https://supabase.com/pricing" class="underline transition underline-offset-2 decoration-inherit hover:decoration-foreground text-inherit hover:text-foreground">Pricing</a> pages.</p></div><div class="w-full min-w-full sticky top-32 self-start"><p>Additional links</p><ul>
